primary_claim: Evaluation awareness, measured via linear probes on residual-stream activations, scales predictably with model size following a power-law trend, consistently across four open-weight model families spanning 0.27B to 70B parameters.

effect.value: power-law increase in AUROC with model size across 15 models, 0.27B-70B

contradicts_or_qualifies: Qwen models fail to follow the hypothesized increase in evaluation awareness with model size and peak at different relative layer depths than other families, so were excluded from the main analysis
limitations_stated: Mixture-of-Experts architectures make it difficult to establish consistent scaling trends across model families
Several state-of-the-art frontier models are proprietary/black-box, limiting ability to validate whether patterns hold in the most advanced models
quote: Figure 1 illustrates that evaluation awareness scales predictably with model size, following a power-law trend.
